# Policymaker #168, start of iteration 0016

**What I found.** Iteration 0015 closed without a repeat of the 0014 tokenless failure. Re-review #166 ([report](../.github/loop/data/session-reports/166/d35c2aaccdbdd51388cd899e11210fe2788a0b7f8b9cb49663f154c10d98782c.json)) marked F1 and F2 closed at 2669ec4 and recommended **accept**. One caveat: the reviewer fell back to codex/gpt-6.1-sol, the same model family as author #150, so this review is not cross-family. The `tasks`, `oracle`, `split`, `baseline` and `challenges` milestones are still `not-started`. `evaluate.py --check` passes, which only confirms the index is intact: `benchmark_ready=false`, coverage is incomplete and quality is unmeasured.

**Order placed (`order-168-dev-case-specs`, benchmark, default model, high effort, 90 min / 60 turns).** It asks for the first public development cases. They cover the families whose structure can be read from XML (.lvproj, .lvclass, .lvlib), plus one .vi case whose native oracle is explicitly `unavailable`. The cases come from a reproducible `benchmark/scripts/dev_cases.py` with a `--check` mode, include lineage groups for a later split, are pinned under `tasks`/`oracle`, and are marked prepared-not-reviewed. Expected gain: the first real evidence for `tasks`/`oracle`, which `evaluation.md` requires before the owner can judge the method. Check next session: the generator's `--check` exits 0, the case counts per family, the native-unavailable items, and the updated preparation-status.json.

**Request filed (`capability`).** This is row 2 of `benchmark/resources-proposal.md`: bounded read-only native inspection on the existing NI 2026 Q1 container path. It covers public development artifacts only, needs no new spending and no secrets, and has a readiness check stricter than "it compiles". It unblocks native references for the oracle, fidelity probes and challenges. It does not block the order above. I did not file row 1 (restricted store) because it first needs owner answers (which store and who is custodian). I will ask those when split work comes up.

**Not done on purpose.** I have not asked the owner to accept the method yet. The protocol has no evidence behind it so far, and `evaluation.md` requires evidence before acceptance.

Working memory has been updated: [policy/working-memory.md](../policy/working-memory.md). Engine-change #165 is still pending.

## Discoveries
- History records are named with 4 digits (`records/0015.json`), not `15.json`. I recorded this in working memory ([manifest](history/manifest.json)).
- Codex counts all non-cached input: reviewer #166 used 320k input tokens over 19 turns, which matters for quota per accepted result ([record 0015](history/records/0015.json)).

## What next
- Read the benchmark session's report. If it is done, order a review of the cases against protocol `## tasks`, preferring a Claude-family reviewer. If it is partial, let the successor run.
- Start native-reference work only after the capability request has been decided and `capability-ready` is posted.
- Do not re-read the protocol or resources-proposal for decisions already in memory.

Waiting for the iteration to continue: then `policy/` merges and the orders start.
